WITH film_lengths AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(length) as avg_length
  FROM film
  WHERE length IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rating
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(length) as baseline_length
  FROM film
  WHERE length IS NOT NULL
),
above_baseline AS (
  SELECT fl.rating, fl.avg_length
  FROM film_lengths fl
  CROSS JOIN baseline b
  WHERE fl.avg_length > b.baseline_length
),
mean_above_baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_length) as mean_above_baseline
  FROM above_baseline
),
final_ratings AS (
  SELECT ab.rating, ab.avg_length
  FROM above_baseline ab
  CROSS JOIN mean_above_baseline mab
  WHERE ab.avg_length > mab.mean_above_baseline
)
SELECT
  AVG(fr.avg_length) as mean_of_remaining,
  AVG(fr.avg_length - b.baseline_length) as mean_excess_over_baseline,
  AVG(fr.avg_length - mab.mean_above_baseline) as mean_excess_over_kept_mean
FROM final_ratings fr
CROSS JOIN baseline b
CROSS JOIN mean_above_baseline mab

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the average length computed over individual films (AVG of all film lengths), not the average of rating-group averages. This ensures each film counts equally as stated.

When computing 'the mean amount by which they exceed the kept ratings' mean', the reference is to the mean of ratings above the baseline (computed before the second filter), not the mean of the final set. Using the final set's mean would always yield zero excess, which is uninformative.
If no ratings satisfy both filter thresholds, the query returns NULL values. The request does not specify behavior for this edge case.
